A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAGE and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original SAGE benchmark results, component ablations, descriptor-dimension experiments, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds mining-runtime comparisons, early-training results, threshold sensitivity experiments, SF-small evaluation, and failure examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the DINOv2/DPN backbone adaptation, SoftP, InteractHead, online geo-visual graph creation, and greedy weighted sampling procedures. Newly specified threshold values document existing parameters; no algorithm or architecture change is established.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds evaluation on SF-small, derived from SF-XL and described as using queries from distinct, non-adjacent locations. This extends geographic and query coverage while retaining the original eight evaluation benchmarks and MSLS/GSV-Cities training coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds R2Former, single-stage SelaVPR with 1024-dimensional descriptors, and EDTformer. Appendix Table 13 adds VLAD-BuFF and EffoVPR comparisons on retained benchmarks. These substantially expand the evaluated comparator set while preserving the earlier baseline rows.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes Eynsham's matching threshold from 5 to 25 meters. Table 1 changes Tokyo24/7's database count from 76,112 to 75,984, AmsterTime's database/query counts from 2,710 each to 1,231 each, and Eynsham's from 22,605 each to 23,935 each. V2 also adds online/offline timing controls, epoch-2/4 comparisons, threshold sweeps, and R@5/R@10 reporting for the InteractHead ablation. The PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun under the revised descriptions.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, descriptor sweeps, and successful retrieval visualizations, v2 adds online-versus-offline mining cost and accuracy analysis (Table 7), early convergence against Cliquemining (Table 8), geographic/affinity threshold sensitivity (Table 12), and explicit retrieval failures (Figure 6). These substantially broaden examination of the method's efficiency, robustness, and failure behavior.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates; the retained mathematical variance discussion is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing recall entries are retained numerically, but v2 adds numerous benchmark and analysis results. Table 11 reports SF-small R@1 of 89.3 for SAGE versus 88.2 for EMVP. Table 7 reports online/offline SAGE R@1 of 98.9/98.5 on SPED and 94.5/94.2 on MSLS-val. Table 13 introduces a comparison where EffoVPR exceeds SAGE on Tokyo24/7 R@1, 98.7 versus 97.5. These are added findings, not demonstrated version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same residual weighting, approximate variance argument and assumptions, descriptor transformation, affinity definition, greedy selection rules, and intra-class-distance definition. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, four contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions, parameter-efficiency claims, eight-benchmark SOTA claim, and headline recall values. The additional experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new threshold sweeps as showing limited sensitivity near the selected values and explicitly discusses failures under extreme viewpoint and illumination changes. It qualifies the expanded comparison by acknowledging EffoVPR's higher Tokyo24/7 R@1 while emphasizing reranking overhead. Appendix A.5's existing limitations and future-work discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies geographic and affinity thresholds of 25 meters and -2.88 × 10^3. It changes the reported EMVP implementation provenance from reproducing the authors' source code to reproducing the publication because official code is unavailable. V2 supplies mining/training timings and additional baseline links, but removes the explicit AmsterTime unique-pair matching rule. The abstract replaces SAGE's promised repository URL with release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces broad criticism of VFM resource demands with a distinction between encoder tuning and PEFT. Related Work adds discussion and citations including Visual Prompt Tuning, MegaLoc, SuperPlace, EmbodiedPlace, and D2-VPR; Appendix A.4 expands baseline descriptions. Some references, including StructVPR++ and GhostVLAD, are removed. The central positioning around dynamic versus static sampling remains.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the introduction, related work, implementation paragraph, and appendix dataset descriptions, alongside explanations of the added experiments. Terminology is refined, including SPED's expansion and graph-creation wording. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds five tables (7, 8, 11–13) and a failure-case figure (6), substantially expanding the empirical displays. Table 2 gains comparator rows, Table 6 gains recall columns, and Tables 1 and 6 move. Earlier appendix Figures 6–8 and Tables 7–8 are retained as Figures 7–9 and Tables 9–10.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens assessment of the central sampling claim through direct online/offline cost-and-accuracy comparisons and early-training evidence, supplemented by threshold sensitivity and failure examples. These make the paper more informative and balanced. The net gain is limited because revised dataset counts and Eynsham criteria are not reconciled with retained scores, EMVP implementation provenance changes without explanation, and SAGE's release information becomes less concrete.
